criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear goal, four numbered objectives/requirements, and named users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) with needs explicitly mapped to objectives. Rationale is well referenced. Minor: [6] is a NOAA page cited for BoM SST products, and [4] is a news article rather than the primary method paper.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days
The satellite would be operated by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS).

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart with completed/planned coding and deadlines, per-task descriptions, a risk/contingency table with triggers and responses, and a sources table. Plan is explicitly justified against the mission sequence (orbit before comms, EOL after orbit). Robust and feasible.

evidence.quote: The order follows the mission: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time
Week 10 is float as well as editing time: no new design work is planned in it.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Hand calculations for a, T, orbits/day, SSO inclination, ground-track shift and swath are all numerically correct (T=5801 s, 14.9 rev/day, 24.2 deg, 60 km). Interpretation identifies the swath/coverage trade and links it to a contingency. STK work is only just started, so progress is good but early.

evidence.quote: the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes
A first STK scenario with this orbit has been set up, and its period agrees with the hand calculation.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, clear headings, professional prose, consistent formatting. Figure 1 and Tables 1-3 are labelled and captioned. All eleven references are cited in text and appear in the list in a consistent style. Only minor citation-content mismatches.

evidence.quote: Table 2 lists the sources I plan to use and what each is for.
[7] J. R. Wertz, D. F. Everett, and J. J. Puschell, Eds., Space Mission Engineering: The New SMAD.

technical_issues.issue: Reference [6] (NOAA climate-change page) is cited as the source for the Bureau of Meteorology combining imagery with SST products; citation does not support the claim.
Objective 2 is to be refined against [4], but [4] is a Nature news article, not the primary Asner method paper; the 10 m GSD requirement is therefore not traceable to a technical source.
'Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic' is a simplification; the underlying change is a ~0.1 pH-unit drop (~30% rise in H+ concentration).
The 97.8 deg sun-synchronous inclination is stated without showing the J2 nodal-precession calculation, so the key result is unverifiable from the report.
The 60 km swath assumes 6,000 cross-track pixels but no detector/pixel-size justification is given, and the 250 km reef width is not referenced.

overall: Strong, well-structured preliminary report. Mission concept, users and requirements are clear and referenced; the Gantt chart, contingencies and source table form a credible plan; hand calculations are correct and interpreted. Main gaps are a few citation-content mismatches and limited STK work to date.

feedback.summary: Your preliminary report is strong and well structured: the mission concept, users and requirements are clear and referenced, your Gantt chart, contingencies and source table form a credible plan, and your hand calculations are correct and interpreted. The main gaps are a few citation–content mismatches and limited STK work so far. Addressing the next steps will move you from 9 to 10 within the Accomplished band.
next_steps: Fix the citation–content mismatches in Mission Concept & Rationale: replace [6] with a source that actually supports BoM combining imagery with SST products, and cite the primary Asner method paper rather than news article [4] so the 10 m GSD requirement is traceable.

In Preliminary Progress, show the J2 nodal-precession calculation behind the 97.8° sun-synchronous inclination, and justify the 60 km swath from the 6,000 cross-track pixels/detector pixel size, referencing the 250 km reef width.
Extend the STK work beyond the first scenario—ground tracks, coverage and revisit—so your preliminary progress is clearly on track for completion.

criteria.C1: You set a clear goal, four numbered objectives and named users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) with needs mapped to objectives, and the rationale is well referenced. For full marks, replace [6] with a source that actually supports BoM combining imagery with SST products, cite the primary Asner method paper instead of news article [4] so the 10 m GSD is traceable, and correct '30% more acidic' to the ~0.1 pH-unit drop.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart with completed/planned coding and deadlines, per-task descriptions, risk/contingency table with triggers and responses, and sources table make a robust, feasible plan. You justify the order against the mission sequence (orbit before comms, EOL after orbit) and build in Week 10 float. To secure full marks, make each contingency trigger and source-to-task link explicit in the Gantt so the plan's robustness is visible at a glance.
criteria.C3: Your hand calculations are correct (T=5801 s, 14.9 rev/day, 24.2°, 60 km), and you interpret the swath/coverage trade and link it to a contingency; your first STK scenario's period agrees. For full marks, show the J2 nodal-precession calculation behind the 97.8° inclination, justify the 6,000 cross-track pixels/pixel size for the 60 km swath and reference the 250 km reef width, and extend STK to ground tracks, coverage and revisit.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear, logical structure with headings, professional prose and consistent formatting; Figure 1 and Tables 1–3 are labelled and captioned, and all eleven references are cited in text and listed consistently. To reach full marks, resolve the citation–content mismatches in Mission Concept & Rationale so every in-text citation supports its claim, and keep the same citation discipline as you add STK results.
